chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said:

I asked him about a man who sees the crescent in the month of Ramadan alone, and no one else sees it with him, whether he may fast. He said: 'If he is not doubtful about it, let him fast; otherwise, let him fast with the people.'

key_terms.الْهِلَالُ: The crescent moon, used to determine the start of lunar months like Ramadan.
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramadan, the month of fasting.
key_terms.مَعَ النَّاسِ: With the people/community, implying following the general consensus or official sighting.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who sees the Ramadan crescent alone?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Kazim, the distinction is drawn between personal certainty (yaqin) and communal consensus (ijma') regarding lunar sighting, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that individual certainty can suffice for starting Ramadan but doubt necessitates alignment with the majority to preserve unity. This ruling highlights the balance between individual religious obligation and social cohesion in Shia fiqh, particularly within the framework of the Taqdir (calculation) and Ru'yah (sighting) debates.
